reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an apparently easy ETH-generation method through a flash-loan arbitrage contract and directs viewers to fund the contract with ETH for arbitrage and fees. It demonstrates sending one ETH to the contract address and reports an increase to 1.3 ETH, while the available records do not establish whether the return or transfer was genuine.

citations.quote: How To Make ETH With Uniswap in 2023 - No Code Flash Loan (For Beginners)
Today I want to share with you how to deploy your own flashloan arbitrage bot on the ethereum mainnet, which can help you to make a passive income in ether.
As we have an infinite amount of our own coins, we can generate substantial amounts of Ethereum in a swap.
my recommendation is at least 0.5 because the smartcontract will use the ether to perform the flash loan arbitrage and to cover fees for that.
send one ether to this address

opening.argument: The presentation includes material risk disclosures that are inconsistent with representing ETH generation as certain or effortless. The description expressly says the arbitrage might fail when contract ETH is depleted and explains that insufficient ETH can cause the borrowing or flash loan to fail because of interest or gas costs. It also identifies volatility and funding as variables affecting the result. Those qualifications frame the method as conditional and technically risky, not as a guaranteed return.

citations.quote: IMPORTANT: the arbitrage might fail due to depletion of ETH in your smart contract as gas price varies from time to time.
If you dont put the enough ETH the borrow and the flashloan might fail due to the interest to be paid at the end of the flash loans or transaction gas cost.
Higher the volatility, higher profit due to price change.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference emphasizes funding and the reported result, but those points do not establish a guaranteed or risk-free promise. The same material warns that the operation can fail and that gas, interest, volatility, and contract depletion affect the outcome. Sending ETH to cover execution costs is therefore presented alongside explicit conditions, not as proof that every viewer will receive a return.

citations.quote: the arbitrage might fail due to depletion of ETH in your smart contract
The gas fees are usually very high
It is recommended to fund the contract with around 0.2 ETH to make sure that it has sufficient funding for gas fees

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not change the central conduct being promoted. The speaker still tells viewers to deploy the contract, fund it with ETH, activate it, and reports an increase from one ETH to 1.3 ETH. A disclaimer about possible failure can make a solicitation more qualified without showing that the underlying return claim is reliable.

we started with one ether and now we are actually at 1.3 ETH

opening.argument: The video's observable structure is an operational technology tutorial: it walks through installing MetaMask, opening Remix, creating a file, pasting a smart-contract program, compiling it, deploying it, and using the interface. The narration repeatedly describes procedural steps rather than presenting a passive investment product. The sampled frames likewise show MetaMask and the Remix development environment, supporting an instructional demonstration of blockchain tooling.

citations.quote: First, you need to download the metamask extension from the official website.
We head over to Remix.Then we go to Deploy and run transactions
we make a new file and name it call ether flash loan
we go to the solidity compiler and our smart contract runs on version 0.5.0 plus commit and then we can hit the compile button

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference reads the tutorial steps as solicitation, but procedural instruction is not itself proof of deception. The recording explains how to connect a wallet, compile code, and deploy a contract in a development interface. Its claim about the displayed outcome is a demonstration report; the available material does not independently establish that it was fabricated or that viewers were promised the same result.

citations.quote: Then we go to Deploy and run transactions.
we can hit the compile button

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not answer what the tutorial teaches viewers to do. It is specifically framed as a bot that can make passive ETH income, and the steps culminate in sending ETH to the deployed contract and activating the arbitrage. The presence of a code editor shows technical presentation, but it does not show that the income claim is merely educational or that the demonstrated transaction is independently verified.

opening.argument: The material describes a software and smart-contract workflow, not a conventional deposit scheme or recruitment program. It provides code and development resources, directs users to MetaMask and Remix, and explains that ETH is needed for contract funding and transaction costs. The supplied content contains no request for account credentials, no downline or referral-income structure, and no stated guarantee that deposited ETH will be returned. The existence of a financial outcome claim does not by itself establish those missing scam mechanisms.

the smartcontract will use the ether to perform the flash loan arbitrage and to cover fees for that.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference identifies ETH funding, but funding a contract for gas and arbitrage is not the same as asking for credentials, recruiting others, or guaranteeing repayment. The supplied material describes where code and development tools are accessed and acknowledges that the transaction can fail. Without evidence of a concealed fee, credential capture, or guaranteed return, the mechanism remains a disclosed technical workflow.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing mechanisms listed by the defense are not necessary to establish this category. The relevant conduct is an invitation to deploy and fund a contract for claimed ETH profit. The speaker recommends substantial ETH funding, instructs a transfer to the contract, and reports a 30 percent increase, while the supplied record does not verify that the increase was genuine or repeatable.
